name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
flagName: Flag of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
summary: A blue, white and red horizontal tricolour with a large red star edged in gold in the centre. The Pan-Slavic tricolour of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia was given a communist star by Tito's partisans.
origin: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (from 1929 the Kingdom of Yugoslavia) used a blue-white-red tricolour, the Pan-Slavic colours.

During the Second World War, Josip Broz Tito's partisans added a red star. The star-and-tricolour became the flag of the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia under its 1946 constitution, and continued under the Socialist Federal Republic from 1963.

After Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia declared independence in 1991–1992, Serbia and Montenegro formed the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and used the tricolour without the star.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The Pan-Slavic colours of the South Slav peoples.

symbols.name: Red star
symbols.description: A large five-pointed red star bordered in gold, overlapping all three bands.
symbols.meaning: Socialism and the partisan struggle in the Second World War.

history.label: Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
history.note: Serbia and Montenegro; tricolour without the star.

facts: Each of the six republics had its own flag, mostly national tricolours with the red star.
The star's points touch all three bands, so the star overlaps blue, white and red.
Serbia's flag uses red-blue-white, the Yugoslav colours in a different order.
clues: Blue, white and red bands with a large red star edged in gold across them.
Partisans added its star during the Second World War.
Its federation broke apart in 1991–1992, leaving two republics to keep the plain tricolour.
Its six republics each had their own star-bearing flags.
